findings.description: Return value of ISkyPSM(psm).buyGem(address(this), gemAmt) is ignored. The donated USDC amount is assumed to equal the locally-computed gemAmt rather than read from the PSM. The subsequent forceApprove(streamer, gemAmt) + collectNudge(batchMinter, gem, gemAmt) are sized on the computed value, so a PSM that delivers less than gemAmt would make collectNudge pull more than was received (or revert on insufficient balance).

Return value (shares minted) of IERC4626(_sUSDS).deposit(poolingUSDS, address(this)) is ignored. Downstream pool() re-reads balanceOf(_sUSDS) rather than trusting a share count, which mitigates this, but no minimum-shares check exists on the wrap leg.

Return value of IBalancerVault(_vault).unlock(data) is ignored. The unlock return carries the callback's ABI-encoded return data; a failure inside the callback reverts, so the practical impact is limited.

Return value of IBalancerVault(_vault).settle(IERC20(_sUSDS), actualInVault) is ignored (line 395); addLiquidity at line 394 discards all tuple members except bptAmountOut. bptAmountOut is slippage-checked against minBPT, so the addLiquidity leg is guarded; the settle credit is not verified.

gemAmt = (usdsAmount * WAD) / (conv * (WAD + tout)) at line 322 is then multiplied back at line 331 (usdsSpent = gemAmt * conv * (WAD + tout) / WAD). Ordering appears deliberate and is documented in-code as a FLOOR so dust accrues to the protocol and never over-credits; flagged for confirmation that the floor direction is truly protocol-favourable in all tout regimes.
Dangerous strict equality `sUSDSAmount == 0` on a token balance. View-only helper; impact depends on whether callers use getIdealBPT to size a slippage floor.

BatchDonatedViaPSM is emitted after the external buyGem + collectNudge calls. Event-ordering only; no state write follows the external calls. Relevant to the story-047 review because collectNudge is a NEW external call inside this envelope — Slither found NO reentrancy-eth / reentrancy-no-eth on this path.
Pooled event emitted after addLiquidity/settle external calls. Event-ordering only.

Three ignored returns in pool(): swapExactTokensForTokens (line 276), swapExactTokensForTokens (line 289), addLiquidity (line 302, only `liquidity` retained). minPairOut / minTargetOut / minLP slippage floors are applied, which mitigates; the swap amountsOut arrays are never inspected.

block.timestamp used as the UniswapV2 router deadline (lines 276, 289) — an inline block.timestamp deadline provides no MEV/staleness protection since it is always satisfiable at inclusion time. Also flagged: require(liquidity >= minLP) at line 305 under Slither's block-dependency detector. NOT dropped (protocol is time-driven; per run policy timestamp findings survive to dedup).

Ignored returns from swapExactTokensForETH (line 504) and swapExactETHForTokens (line 510). minEthOut / minPromoOut floors are supplied, so the swaps are slippage-guarded; the returned amounts arrays are discarded rather than used to size the subsequent leg.

addLiquidity(phUSD, promotionToken, phusdBal, promoBal, 0, 0, this, block.timestamp) discards amountA/amountB and passes ZERO as both amountAMin and amountBMin. The only guard is the post-hoc require(liquidity >= minLP) at line 471. Zero min-amounts on an AMM add is the highest-signal item on the changed contracts — worth manual confirmation that minLP alone bounds the ratio exposure.
IBalancerVault.swap(p) tuple partially discarded (line 561) and IBalancerVault.settle(IERC20(sUSDS), sharesIn) return ignored (line 562).

nonReentrant is not the first modifier, so preceding modifiers execute outside the reentrancy guard. Instances: BalancerPoolerV2.sol:356 (onlyAuthorizedPooler, whenNotPaused precede), NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.sol:108, PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:429, Uniboost.sol:270, BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.sol:120, NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook.sol:136, UniboostMintDebtHook.sol:141. Exploitable only if a preceding modifier makes an external call — none observed.

Specifically on the story-046/047 INudgeStreamer.collectNudge hop in all four changed dispatchers: no reentrancy detector fired, and no unchecked-transfer/arbitrary-from detector fired on the forceApprove -> collectNudge sequence.

The nudgeStreamer zero-address concern is NOT flagged by any tool because every call site has an explicit `require(streamer != address(0), "<C>: nudgeStreamer unset")` immediately before use, and every setNudgeStreamer rejects address(0).
handoffNotes: SAST BLIND SPOT (for code-scanner/econ-scanner, not a tool finding): all four dispatchers approve the streamer with forceApprove(streamer, amount) and rely on the in-code assertion that 'collectNudge consumes the whole allowance in this same transaction'. That is an assumption about an EXTERNAL contract (phoenix-nft-staking NudgeStreamer) that no static tool can verify. If a streamer implementation ever pulls less than the approved amount, a residual allowance persists on a USDC-class token. Worth a manual check against the NudgeStreamer source.

SAST BLIND SPOT: BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch wraps the donation in `try this._psmDonate() {} catch { emit DonationSkipped(...) }`. Story 047 deliberately placed the streamer hop INSIDE this envelope, so a streamer misconfiguration (unset, NotRegistered, NotWhitelisted) silently parks USDS and emits DonationSkipped rather than reverting. This is documented as intentional but is a swallow-the-revert path a static tool cannot rank — hand to the story-faithfulness and econ scanners.

SAST BLIND SPOT: the other three dispatchers do NOT wrap collectNudge in try/catch — a streamer misconfiguration there BRICKS dispatch outright. The asymmetry between BalancerPoolerV2 (silent park) and NudgeRatchet/Uniboost/PromotionUniV2_Eth (hard revert) is a deliberate design split per the dev comments, but is worth confirming as intended.
